## 1. Purpose

This procedure describes bench-top measurement of pH and specific
conductance (conductivity) in water samples, soil extracts, and other
aqueous solutions using a laboratory pH/conductivity meter. Accurate
pH and conductivity measurements are fundamental to water quality
assessment and are referenced by multiple analytical SOPs throughout the
EA Program [@apha2012; @eaton2005].


## 2. Scope

- **Applies to:** Bench-top pH and specific conductance measurements
  on surface water, groundwater, wastewater, soil-water extracts
  (e.g., 1:1 or 1:5 soil slurries), KCl extracts (see
  [SOP-L57](SOP-L57-nitrate-ammonium-kcl.qmd)), and reagent solutions
- **Does not apply to:** Field measurements using portable multiprobes
  (see [SOP-F22 Eureka Manta2](../field_sops/SOP-F22-eureka-manta2.qmd));
  continuous monitoring or in-situ deployments
- **Location:** EA Program laboratory, SGM 133


## 3. Responsibilities

| Role              | Responsibility                              |
|:------------------|:--------------------------------------------|
| Lab PI            | Approve SOP, ensure training compliance     |
| Lab Manager       | Maintain meter and electrodes, stock buffer solutions |
| Trained Personnel | Calibrate meter before each session, measure and record results |
| New Students      | Complete training before independent use    |


## 4. Safety and Hazards

::: {.callout-warning}
### Hazards

- **Chemical:** pH buffer solutions (pH 4, 7, 10) are mild irritants.
  Conductivity standards contain dissolved salts. KCl electrode fill
  solution is a mild irritant. Acidic or alkaline samples may cause
  skin or eye irritation.
- **Electrical:** Keep the meter and power supply away from water spills
  on the bench.
:::

### Required PPE

- [ ] Nitrile gloves
- [ ] Safety glasses
- [ ] Lab coat

### Emergency Procedures

For buffer or sample splashes to eyes, flush with water at the eyewash
station for at least 15 minutes. For skin contact, wash with soap and
water. Refer to
[SOP-L01 Laboratory Safety](SOP-L01-laboratory-safety.qmd).


## 5. Equipment and Materials

### Equipment

| Item                              | Location         | Notes                          |
|:----------------------------------|:-----------------|:-------------------------------|
| pH/conductivity meter             | Lab bench, SGM 133 | *TBD -- confirm model (e.g., Accumet AB150, Orion Star, or equivalent)* |
| pH electrode (combination glass)  | Stored in pH 4 or KCl storage solution | Replace annually or when response time degrades |
| Conductivity cell (2- or 4-electrode) | Stored dry or in DI water | Cell constant typically 1.0 cm^-1^ |
| Magnetic stir plate and stir bars | Lab bench        | Optional, for large-volume samples |
| Temperature probe (ATC)           | Built into meter or separate | For automatic temperature compensation |

### Standards and Consumables

| Item                                  | Notes                              |
|:--------------------------------------|:-----------------------------------|
| pH buffer 4.01 (red)                  | NIST-traceable; store at room temperature |
| pH buffer 7.00 (yellow)              | NIST-traceable; store at room temperature |
| pH buffer 10.01 (blue)               | NIST-traceable; store at room temperature |
| Conductivity standard (1413 uS/cm)   | KCl-based; store at room temperature |
| Conductivity standard (84 uS/cm or 12,880 uS/cm) | For low- or high-range verification |
| KCl electrode fill solution (3 M or saturated) | For refilling the reference junction |
| DI water (Type I or II)              | For rinsing electrodes between samples |
| Lint-free wipes (Kimwipes)           | For blotting electrodes             |
| Small beakers or sample cups (50--100 mL) | Clean, for holding aliquots    |


## 6. Procedure

### 6.1 Electrode Preparation

1. Remove the pH electrode from its storage solution. Inspect the glass
   bulb for cracks, chips, or deposits. If the bulb is damaged, replace
   the electrode.
2. If the electrode has a refillable reference junction, check the KCl
   fill level. Refill to the indicated line with 3 M KCl or saturated
   KCl solution if low. Open the fill hole during measurements to allow
   proper electrolyte flow [@rundle2011].
3. Rinse the pH electrode thoroughly with DI water and blot gently with
   a Kimwipe. Do not rub the glass bulb.
4. Rinse the conductivity cell with DI water and blot dry.

### 6.2 pH Calibration (Three-Point)

Calibrate before each measurement session and whenever the meter has
been turned off [@apha2012].

1. Pour approximately 30--50 mL of each buffer solution into clean,
   labeled beakers. Do not pour used buffer back into the stock bottle.
2. Rinse the pH electrode with DI water and blot gently.
3. Place the electrode into pH 7.00 buffer first. Allow the reading to
   stabilize (stability indicator on the meter display).
4. Accept or set the first calibration point to 7.00.
5. Rinse with DI water, blot, and place into pH 4.01 buffer. Allow to
   stabilize and accept.
6. Rinse with DI water, blot, and place into pH 10.01 buffer. Allow to
   stabilize and accept.
7. The meter should display the slope (ideally 95--102% of theoretical
   Nernstian slope, i.e., approximately 56--60 mV/pH unit at 25 C).
   If the slope falls below 90%, the electrode may need cleaning or
   replacement [@illingworth1981].
8. Record the calibration date, buffer lot numbers, slope, and any
   offset in the meter calibration log.

::: {.callout-tip}
### Tip
Always calibrate starting with pH 7.00, then move to pH 4.01, and
finish with pH 10.01. The 7.00 buffer sets the zero point (offset),
while the acidic and basic buffers define the slope. If you only have
two buffers, bracket the expected sample range (e.g., pH 4 and 7 for
acidic samples, pH 7 and 10 for alkaline samples).
:::

### 6.3 Conductivity Calibration (One-Point)

1. Rinse the conductivity cell with DI water and blot dry
2. Pour approximately 30--50 mL of the 1413 uS/cm standard into a
   clean beaker
3. Immerse the conductivity cell fully in the standard. Tap gently to
   release air bubbles from the cell opening.
4. Allow the reading to stabilize with temperature compensation active
5. Calibrate (adjust the cell constant) so that the display reads
   1413 uS/cm (at 25 C)
6. Record the calibration date and standard lot number in the log
7. *TBD -- if your lab uses a different primary conductivity standard
   (e.g., 84 uS/cm for low-conductivity water or 12,880 uS/cm for
   brackish water), adjust accordingly*

::: {.callout-important}
Never measure conductivity on a water sample that has already been used
for pH measurement. The KCl from the pH electrode reference junction
leaks into the sample and alters conductivity. Always measure
conductivity first, or use a separate aliquot [@apha2012].
:::

### 6.4 Measuring pH

1. Rinse the pH electrode with DI water and blot gently
2. Pour approximately 30--50 mL of the sample into a clean beaker. Use
   a separate aliquot from the one used for conductivity.
3. Immerse the electrode so that the glass bulb and reference junction
   are fully submerged
4. Allow the reading to stabilize (typically 30--60 seconds for
   well-buffered samples; may take 2--3 minutes for low-ionic-strength
   water)
5. Record the pH value, sample temperature, and sample ID in the lab
   notebook
6. Rinse the electrode with DI water between samples

### 6.5 Measuring Conductivity

1. Rinse the conductivity cell with DI water and blot dry
2. Pour approximately 30--50 mL of the sample into a clean beaker
3. Immerse the cell fully. Tap gently to dislodge air bubbles.
4. Allow the reading to stabilize
5. Record the specific conductance (uS/cm at 25 C), sample temperature,
   and sample ID in the lab notebook
6. Rinse the cell with DI water between samples

### 6.6 Measuring Soil pH and Conductivity (Soil Slurry Method)

For soil pH and electrical conductivity, prepare a soil-water slurry
[@thomas1996; @rhoades1996]:

1. Weigh 10 g of air-dried, sieved (2 mm) soil into a clean beaker
2. Add 10 mL of DI water for a 1:1 soil-water ratio (or 50 mL for a
   1:5 ratio, depending on the protocol). Record the ratio used.
3. Stir the slurry vigorously for 30 seconds, then allow to stand for
   10 minutes
4. Stir again briefly, then insert the pH electrode into the slurry
   while it is still suspended. Allow to stabilize and record.
5. For conductivity, use a separate slurry aliquot or prepare a fresh
   slurry. Insert the conductivity cell into the supernatant after the
   soil has settled. Record.
6. See also *SOP-L57 Soil pH and Salinity* for additional detail.

### 6.7 Electrode Storage and Maintenance

1. After use, rinse the pH electrode with DI water and return it to its
   storage solution (pH 4 buffer or KCl storage solution as recommended
   by the manufacturer). Never store the pH electrode dry or in DI
   water, as this damages the glass membrane [@illingworth1981].
2. Store the conductivity cell dry or in DI water (per manufacturer
   recommendation).
3. If the pH electrode response becomes sluggish (stabilization takes
   more than 3 minutes) or the calibration slope drops below 90%,
   soak the electrode in electrode cleaning solution or dilute HCl
   (0.1 M) for 15--30 minutes, rinse with DI water, and recalibrate.
4. Replace the pH electrode if the slope remains below 90% after
   cleaning or if the glass bulb is cracked.


## 7. Quality Control and Acceptance Criteria

- Calibrate the pH meter before each measurement session using a
  three-point calibration
- Calibrate the conductivity meter before each session using a
  traceable standard
- Acceptable pH calibration slope: 90--102% of theoretical Nernstian
  slope (approximately 54--60 mV/pH at 25 C)
- Check calibration by re-reading pH 7.00 buffer after every 10
  samples. If the reading has drifted by more than +/- 0.05 pH units,
  recalibrate.
- Check conductivity by re-reading the 1413 uS/cm standard after every
  10 samples. If the reading has drifted by more than +/- 5%,
  recalibrate.
- Run duplicate measurements on at least 10% of samples. Acceptable
  precision: +/- 0.1 pH units and +/- 5% for conductivity.
- Record all calibration data, standard lot numbers, electrode
  condition, and QC check results in the meter log.


## 8. Waste Disposal

| Waste Type                 | Disposal Method                          |
|:---------------------------|:-----------------------------------------|
| Used pH buffer solutions   | Collect in waste container; do not pour down the drain |
| Used conductivity standard | Drain with copious water (KCl solutions are non-hazardous) |
| Soil slurry waste          | Standard trash (if non-hazardous soil)   |
| Spent KCl fill solution    | Drain with copious water                 |
| DI water rinses            | Drain                                    |

## 10. Training Record

Before measuring pH and conductivity independently, personnel must:

1. Read this SOP and [SOP-L01 Laboratory Safety](SOP-L01-laboratory-safety.qmd)
   in full
2. Demonstrate a three-point pH calibration with acceptable slope
3. Demonstrate a one-point conductivity calibration
4. Perform measurements on at least 5 practice samples under
   supervision with acceptable duplicate precision
5. Demonstrate proper electrode storage
6. Be signed off by the PI or lab manager


## Appendix A: Troubleshooting {.appendix}

| Symptom                          | Probable Cause                     | Corrective Action                          |
|:---------------------------------|:-----------------------------------|:-------------------------------------------|
| pH reading drifts and does not stabilize | Fouled or aging electrode; depleted KCl fill | Clean electrode; refill KCl; replace if slope is below 90% |
| Calibration slope below 90%      | Electrode aging or contamination   | Soak in cleaning solution; replace if unresponsive |
| pH buffer reads correctly but samples do not stabilize | Low ionic strength sample | Allow extra stabilization time (up to 5 min); consider adding ionic strength adjuster |
| Conductivity reads zero          | Air bubble in cell; broken cell    | Tap cell to dislodge bubbles; inspect for cracks |
| Conductivity reading too high on all samples | Contaminated cell or residual standard | Rinse cell thoroughly with DI water; recalibrate |
| Conductivity standard reads correctly but samples seem wrong | Temperature compensation off or incorrect cell constant | Verify ATC is enabled; recalibrate cell constant |
